THE HON MR JUSTICE JOSEPH FOK: Mr J C H Ho (Stipendiary Steward)
STAR BROSE: On jumping shifted in and made contact with OCEAN IMPACT.  Shifted out near the 450 Metres and was bumped.  Sent for sampling post-race.
MASSIVE GLORY: Near the 2100 Metres became unbalanced when it made contact with  OCEAN IMPACT due to OCEAN IMPACT shifting in slightly and YOUNG FIGHTER shifting out.
GRAND TURBO: Near the 450 Metres shifted out when bumped by STAR BROSE which shifted out to commence a forward move.  Approaching the 300 Metres raced in restricted room between KASA PAPA and OCEAN IMPACT which shifted to the outside of PERFECT PAIRING.  L Hewitson stated that he was given no specific instructions and to ride his mount depending on how it jumped.  He said when the horse commenced well tonight he was able to hold an on-pace position.
OCEAN IMPACT: Bumped at the start.  Shifted in near the 2100 Metres and was bumped.  M Chadwick reported that his mount appeared to race "flat” tonight and, in his opinion, may race best when given more time between runs.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
SHARPEN BRIGHT: Jumped awkwardly.  Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
SMILING ONE: Bumped shortly after the start.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
OUR LUCKY GLORY: J Orman stated that from a wide barrier he was instructed to ride the horse in a conservative manner in the early stages.  Mr C F Wong representing Trainer W Y So, who was not present tonight, confirmed the instructions issued.
YOUNG FIGHTER: Bumped shortly after the start.  When questioned regarding the tactics adopted from the 1000 Metres where K Teetan commenced a forward move, K Teetan stated that he was instructed to hold an on-pace position and not to contest the lead if GOLDEN FORTUNE, the expected leader, went forward.  He said his instructions were also that if the pace of the event was being run outside of standard time he was given the option of making a move in the race as YOUNG FIGHTER is one-paced.  He said after being crossed by GOLDEN FORTUNE in the early stages, near the 1500 Metres he shifted to GOLDEN FORTUNE’s outside when the pace of the event was being run outside of standard time.  He added entering the Back Straight near the 1000 Metres he elected to comply with his instructions and made a forward move as he was of the opinion this would provide his mount with the opportunity to finish in the best possible placing in the race.  He said after improving past GOLDEN FORTUNE near the 900 Metres he then continued to ride his mount along as he was of the opinion by obtaining a break on the field would give his mount the best chance of winning the event.  Mr C K Chung representing Trainer C Fownes, who was not present tonight, confirmed the instructions issued.  Sent for sampling post-race.
SUPER HONG KONG: From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race found that horse to be lame in its right front leg.  Before being allowed to race again, SUPER HONG KONG will be subjected to an official veterinary examination. <19/11/2026 Additional Veterinary Reports>SUPER HONG KONG, which performed disappointingly, was examined by the Veterinary Officer who said at that time the horse was lame in its right front leg. SUPER HONG KONG was again examined by the Veterinary Officer at the stables of Trainer C H Yip this morning. He said at this time he noted the horse to be also lame in its left hind leg. As previously advised, SUPER HONG KONG will be subjected to an official veterinary examination before being allowed to race again.
KASA PAPA: Approaching the 1500 Metres shifted out when being steadied to avoid OCEAN IMPACT.
PERFECT PAIRING: Slow to begin.  Near the 150 Metres was steadied to avoid MASSIVE GLORY which shifted to the outside of GOLDEN FORTUNE.  S Osborne stated that she endeavoured to follow STAR BROSE into the race when that runner commenced a forward move from the 600 Metres, however, PERFECT PAIRING did not respond well to her riding and finished the race off only fairly in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
GOLDEN FRIENDSHIP: Shifted in shortly after the start and was bumped.  Sent for sampling post-race.
MAPOGO: Z Purton stated that his mount led the event as expected and over the final 100 Metres responded only fairly to his riding.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  Sent for sampling post-race.
SPICY SPANGLE: Made contact with GIMME FIVE on jumping due to both runners shifting ground.
TACTICAL COMMAND: Shortly after the start was bumped by GOLDEN FRIENDSHIP which shifted in.  As a result TACTICAL COMMAND was then steadied to avoid LEAN MASTER.
DIAMOND SPARKLE: Became unbalanced when bumped on jumping.  Over the concluding stages was steadied to avoid ALWAYS MY FOLKS (Apprentice H Y Yuen) which shifted in under riding.  Apprentice Yuen was issued with a severe reprimand and advised she must stop riding and straighten her mounts when they shift ground whilst not clear.
ZETA HEDGE: Raced very wide and without cover for the majority of the event.
DIRIYA: On jumping shifted in and became unbalanced when it made contact with DIAMOND SPARKLE.
GIMME FIVE: Made contact with SPICY SPANGLE on jumping due to both runners shifting ground.  Bumped after travelling a short distance.  Near the 350 Metres was steadied when crowded between ZETA HEDGE (H T Mo) which shifted in slightly and GOLDEN FRIENDSHIP which shifted out and away from DIRIYA after being taken out by DIRIYA (R Kingscote) which shifted out.  Both H T Mo and R Kingscote were advised to exercise more care in similar circumstances.
THOUSAND CUPS: After travelling a short distance shifted out slightly and made contact with GIMME FIVE.
SUPER SIXTY: Bumped at the start.  Whilst the Stewards were satisfied that the riding of E C W Wong, 5th placegetter, over the concluding stages did not affect the horse’s finishing position, he was nonetheless reminded of his obligation to ensure that he fully rides his mounts out to the finish of the race.
LUNAR DASH: Prior to the running of the event Mr H W Cheung representing Trainer B Crawford, who was not present tonight, advised that the horse would be ridden forward which was consistent with the manner in which it was ridden at its most recent start.  K Teetan confirmed that from a wide barrier he was instructed to go forward.  He said when under pressure in the Home Straight LUNAR DASH responded only fairly to his riding and gave ground over the final 200 Metres.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race revealed that the horse was displaying an irregular heart rhythm, a condition which had previously been reported on 14.2.26.  Before being allowed to race again, LUNAR DASH will be required to perform satisfactorily in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
AGENT: Near the 300 Metres AGENT endeavoured to improve between NEVER SETTLE and VIGOR EYE where there was not sufficient room to do so.  As a result AGENT was then checked when disappointed for clear running between NEVER SETTLE and VIGOR EYE.
GALLANT TRIUMPH: M Chadwick stated that his mount led the event as expected.  He stated that GALLANT TRIUMPH, which was having its first race start, raced greenly during the event and under pressure in the Home Straight hung in.  Mr P K Lo representing Trainer J Cummings, who was not present tonight, stated that, in his opinion, the horse raced keenly in the early stages when VIGOR EYE was positioned to its outside.  He also confirmed the advice of Jockey Chadwick that the horse had been disadvantaged by racing greenly.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
SPEED BABY: Shifted in at the start and made contact with SUPER SIXTY.
NEVER SETTLE: Shortly after the start became unbalanced when bumped by SHOW ME YOUR LOVE.  Sent for sampling post-race.
STAR OF HEARTS: Jumped only fairly.  When questioned regarding his riding in the Home Straight K C Leung stated that after improving towards the inside near the 300 Metres he observed GALLANT TRIUMPH commencing to give ground.  He said when the winner BETTER AND BETTER improved past him near the 250 Metres he elected to endeavour to follow that runner into the event.  He added after shifting to the outside of SUPER SIXTY to improve he was then disappointed for clear running between SUPER SIXTY and AGENT when both runners shifted ground and as a consequence he was unable to ride his mount out over the final 100 Metres.
BULLISH NOVA: Made contact with a rail on leaving the Parade Ring, was examined by the Veterinary Officer and passed suitable to race.  Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event.
BETTER AND BETTER: From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  Sent for sampling post-race.
SHOW ME YOUR LOVE: SHOW ME YOUR LOVE, which was fractious in the starting gates, jumped only fairly.  Shortly after the start then shifted out and made contact with NEVER SETTLE.  Near the 250 Metres was eased and shifted to the outside of NEVER SETTLE to continue into clear running.
SUPER UNICORN: Jumped awkwardly.  From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.
REFUSETOBEENGLISH: J Orman stated that after following MORGAN SUCCESS, near the 750 Metres his mount made contact with LUCKY TOGETHER.  He said after this incident REFUSETOBEENGLISH, although obliged to race very wide and without cover, failed to respond to his riding from that point.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
MORGAN SUCCESS: A veterinary inspection immediately following the race revealed that the horse was displaying an irregular heart rhythm and an endoscopic examination also showed a substantial amount of blood in its trachea.  Before being allowed to race again, MORGAN SUCCESS will be required to perform satisfactorily in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
WELL ENOUGH: Prior to the running of the event Trainer J Richards confirmed that the intention was to ride the horse in a midfield position with cover.  A Badel stated that when caught wide in the early stages he elected to allow his mount to stride forward and race outside the lead to avoid covering additional ground.  Steadied to avoid RED BRICK WARRIOR near the 200 Metres.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
CLASS: K Teetan (RED BRICK WARRIOR) pleaded guilty to a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that near the 200 Metres he made insufficient effort to prevent RED BRICK WARRIOR from shifting out when insufficiently clear of WELL ENOUGH, resulting in WELL ENOUGH having to be steadied to avoid RED BRICK WARRIOR.  Further he continued to make insufficient effort to prevent RED BRICK WARRIOR from shifting out when insufficiently clear of CLASS, resulting in CLASS having to be checked to avoid RED BRICK WARRIOR.  K Teetan was suspended from riding in races for a period to commence on Wednesday, 25 November 2026 and to expire on Monday, 30 November 2026 on which day he may resume race riding (2 Hong Kong racedays).  In assessing penalty, the Stewards determined the carelessness grade 2 and the consequences grade 2 and also considered his neutral race riding record.
JOY TOGETHER: In the early stages raced keenly and leaving the 1200 Metres was steadied to avoid GAZELEY.  Near the 800 Metres became badly unbalanced and lost ground when it over-reacted to MORGAN SUCCESS shifting in slightly when being corrected by its rider.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
FLYING AMANI: Jumped only fairly.  Briefly held up approaching the 300 Metres.
POET'S REIGN: From the outside barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.
LUCKY TOGETHER: Slow to begin.  Raced keenly in the early stages and near the 1200 Metres was steadied to avoid JOY TOGETHER.  Bumped near the 750 Metres.  Between the 500 Metres and the 350 Metres was held up and unable to improve when positioned between MORGAN SUCCESS and REFUSETOBEENGLISH.
RED BRICK WARRIOR: Jumped awkwardly.  In the Home Straight lay out and proved difficult to ride out.  K Teetan pleaded guilty to a careless riding charge for causing interference near the 200 Metres (see CLASS).  Sent for sampling post-race.
MY DAY MY SAY: From the outside barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.
EVER WEALTH: On jumping shifted out and made contact with FALCON HUNTER.  Noted to have lost its left front plate after the race.  C Y Ho reported that his mount was disadvantaged by being obliged to race wide and without cover for the majority of the event.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
FALCON HUNTER: Bumped at the start.  Sent for sampling post-race.
SPICY BONUS: Jumped only fairly.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
PRIVATE WEALTH: M Chadwick stated that leaving the 1000 Metres, when racing keenly, his saddle shifted forward, placing him at some disadvantage for the remainder of the event.  Sent for sampling post-race.
WORD OF KINDNESS: Jumped only fairly.  After travelling a short distance was eased to avoid EVER WEALTH which shifted in after making contact with FALCON HUNTER.  Near the 500 Metres was momentarily crowded by MY DAY MY SAY which shifted in and away from SPICY BONUS.  H T Mo stated that his mount raced keenly in the early stages and making the first turn leaving the 1000 Metres shifted out and was steadied to avoid MY DAY MY SAY.
SUPERB KING: When questioned Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that the instructions were to go forward and attempt to lead from the outside barrier.  She said despite riding her mount along in the early stages SUPERB KING did not show sufficient pace to comply with those instructions and as a result was left racing very wide and without cover for the majority of the event.  When questioned if there was an opportunity to endeavour to obtain a position with cover behind LOOKING BRIGHT, Apprentice Yuen stated that as SUPERB KING can be one-paced she elected to remain racing to LOOKING BRIGHT’s outside where it was travelling comfortably.  The Stewards advised Apprentice Yuen that, wherever possible, she should endeavour to find a more favourable position closer to the rail to give her mounts the opportunity to obtain the best possible placing in the race.
GEORGIAN SIGMA: Shifted out after travelling a short distance and made contact with EVERSTAR.  Sent for sampling post-race.
PERFECT ONE: Jumped awkwardly and lost ground.  C Y Ho reported that his mount raced greenly throughout the race and failed to respond to his riding in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
HAPPY UNITED: Near the 100 Metres was steadied to avoid SUPERB KING (Apprentice H Y Yuen) which shifted in.  Apprentice Yuen was advised to exercise more care and to stop riding and straighten her mounts sooner than what she did on this occasion.
BOLTZ: After travelling a short distance became unbalanced when bumped by EVERSTAR.
I AM BACK: Jumped only fairly.  From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.
EVERSTAR: After travelling a short distance became unbalanced when crowded between BOLTZ and GEORGIAN SIGMA which shifted out despite the efforts of its rider.
PRESTIGE WIN: Withdrawn on 17.11.26 by order of the Stewards acting on veterinary advice after it was found to be displaying an irregular heart rhythm, a condition which had previously been reported on 12.2.25, and replaced by Standby Declared Starter HAPPY UNITED.  Before being allowed to race again, PRESTIGE WIN will be required to perform satisfactorily in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
MY DAY MY WAY: On jumping was bumped by LIONS SPIRIT which shifted out slightly.  As a result MY DAY MY WAY shifted out and made contact with PRIME SUCCESS.  C L Chau reported that his mount, which was stepping up to 1650 Metres for the first time, raced keenly.  He added the horse would derive benefit from tonight’s race experience.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
PRESTIGE GOOD: In the middle stages raced keenly.  For some distance near the 200 Metres and again near the 100 Metres Apprentice H Y Yuen had difficulty using her whip when positioned close to TURIN CHAMPIONS.  When questioned Apprentice Yuen stated that her instructions were to hold an on-pace position in the first four.  She said after jumping well from her inside barrier she was reluctant to ride her mount along in the early stages as PRESTIGE GOOD has previously raced keenly in its races.  She said having regard to the horse’s racing manners she did not encourage her mount to hold a position initially behind CALL ME TOPSEED and then behind LIONS SPIRIT when LIONS SPIRIT shifted to the rail.  Assistant Trainer Y K Lau confirmed the instructions issued.  After considering her explanation the Stewards advised Apprentice Yuen that in the early stages she had made an error of judgement in not endeavouring to comply with her instructions by firstly attempting to hold a position behind CALL ME TOPSEED and then by allowing her mount to lose ground behind LIONS SPIRIT after LIONS SPIRIT crossed to the rail.  She was further advised in similar circumstances she would be expected to show better judgement than what she did on this occasion.  Sent for sampling post-race.
RIDING TOGETHER: Shortly after the start was bumped by WINDLORD which shifted in.  Raced keenly in the early stages.  After being crossed by WINDLORD approaching the 1400 Metres was steadied to avoid WINDLORD.
HIGHLAND RAHY: L Ferraris reported that his mount lay in throughout the event and came under pressure from the 700 Metres.  He added in the Home Straight HIGHLAND RAHY finished the race off only fairly.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
WROTE A NEW PAGE: Jumped only fairly.  From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.
WINDLORD: Shifted in shortly after the start and was bumped.  Z Purton stated that at its most recent start the horse jumped awkwardly and as a result settled back in the field.  He said his instructions tonight were to endeavour to ensure the horse jumped well and then go forward if circumstances permitted.  Sent for sampling post-race.
AURIO: Shifted out slightly at the start and made contact with GUSTOSISIMO.  Over the concluding stages could not be ridden out when held up behind AURORA LADY.
GREATER BAE: Near the 150 Metres shifted in and made slight contact with VIRTUS GLORY.
ROYAL BLITZ: Prior to the running of the event  Assistant Trainer S H Lee advised the horse would be ridden in a conservative manner in the early stages from its wide barrier, in a similar manner to when it barrier trialed on 6 November 2026.  From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.
AMAZING KID: Noted to have sustained a laceration to the right hind leg after the race.  Sent for sampling post-race.
MAJESTIC ST PAUL'S: Shifted in shortly after the start and made contact with VIRTUS GLORY.
SAINT OF THE SEA: Jumped only fairly.  From the outside barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.
INVINCIBLE STEED: Jumped awkwardly.  In the middle stages raced keenly.  Making the Home Turn was held up behind AMAZING KID and was shifted to the inside of AMAZING KID near the 300 Metres to obtain clear running.
VIRTUS GLORY: Jumped awkwardly and then shortly after the start was crowded by MAJESTIC ST PAUL’S which shifted in despite the efforts of its rider.  Raced keenly in the middle stages.  For a short distance near the 150 Metres raced tight between MAJESTIC ST PAUL’S and GREATER BAE which shifted in and made slight contact with VIRTUS GLORY.  Sent for sampling post-race.
DEVAS TWELVE: Near the 600 Metres lay in and made contact with the running rail.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
THE HEIR: From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.
KYRUS DRAGON: Approaching the 1000 Metres was hampered when taken wider by MALPENSA which shifted out.  Apprentice P N Wong stated that her mount was disadvantaged by being obliged to race wide and without cover for the majority of the event.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
LUCKY RIVER: H Bentley stated that the instructions were to hold a midfield position with cover if possible.  He said in order to comply with the instructions to obtain cover he was obliged to settle further back in the field.
DYNAMIC BROSE: A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
MALPENSA: Shortly after the start shifted in and away from KYRUS DRAGON and made contact with DO YOU JUST.  K Teetan reported that his mount was able to obtain a handy position as expected but raced keenly in the middle stages.  He added that making the Home Turn MALPENSA was taken wider when MEOWTH shifted out to improve and his mount finished the race off only fairly under riding thereafter.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
MEOWTH: Jumped awkwardly, shifted out and made contact with DO YOU JUST.  Raced keenly in the middle stages.
